SYSTEMS PROGRAMMING AND MACHINE ORGANIZATION
Chapter 36 — Memory-Mapped Files
VERBATIM GRADUATE LECTURE TRANSCRIPT
Charles Dorner

SLIDE 1: Chapter 36 — Memory-Mapped Files

LECTURE NARRATION
A memory mapping exposes a file region through virtual addresses. The program accesses bytes with ordinary loads and stores, while the kernel supplies backing pages and enforces mapping permissions. This can simplify random access, but it does not remove I/O, faults, concurrency, or lifetime concerns. [ R14 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a memory mapping exposes a file region through virtual addresses.

SLIDE 4: 36.1 mmap

LECTURE NARRATION
mmap requests a mapping with a length, protection flags, sharing mode, descriptor, and offset. Failure is reported as MAP_FAILED , not as a null pointer. A zero-length mapping is not a valid substitute for handling an empty file. The offset must satisfy the platform’s alignment requirements, normally a multiple of the relevant page size. Mapping an arbitrary record offset often requires rounding the mapping base down to a page boundary and retaining an internal displacement, with overflow checks on the total mapped length.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, mmap requests a mapping with a length, protection flags, sharing mode, descriptor, and offset.

SLIDE 6: 36.2 Address mappings

LECTURE NARRATION
The returned address identifies the beginning of the mapping in the process’s virtual space. Its validity lasts until the mapping is removed or otherwise changed. Closing the original descriptor does not by itself remove an established mapping on Linux. Pointers into the region become invalid after munmap . A function borrowing the mapping must not retain those pointers beyond the owner’s lifetime. Mapping ownership deserves the same discipline as allocation ownership: one clear owner, explicit extent, and structured cleanup.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
Think of an address written on a note: the note can tell you where to look, but it does not prove the thing is still there or that you are allowed to use it.

SLIDE 8: 36.3 File-backed pages

LECTURE NARRATION
File-backed pages associate virtual regions with file contents. A shared writable mapping can propagate modifications to the underlying file according to synchronization and filesystem rules. A private mapping provides private modification semantics instead of updating the file with those writes. Mapping flags are not a complete interprocess synchronization protocol. Multiple writers need an agreed layout and synchronization mechanism. Data-race rules still apply to threads in one process, and process-shared synchronization requires facilities designed for that purpose.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
The program uses a map of memory addresses. The operating system translates that map to where the data is actually stored.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 10: 36.4 Page faults

LECTURE NARRATION
The first access to a mapped page may fault so that the kernel can establish backing. Later accesses can still fault under memory-management activity. A mapping therefore does not promise that every load has register-like or even DRAM-like cost. Concurrent file truncation is a serious hazard. Accessing a mapped region whose backing has been removed can generate SIGBUS on Linux. Checking file size before mapping is not enough when another actor can shrink the file afterward. The example below requires a stable regular file throughout the mapping’s lifetime.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
The program uses a map of memory addresses. The operating system translates that map to where the data is actually stored.

SLIDE 12: 36.5 Mapping permissions

LECTURE NARRATION
Protection flags specify permitted reads, writes, and instruction execution. They must be compatible with the mapping and descriptor’s access rights. A read-only mapping is appropriate for a checksum or parser that does not need to modify the file. Use the least authority required. Do not request writable executable memory merely because it seems convenient. For writable shared file mappings, msync can request synchronization under its documented semantics, while a complete durable-update protocol may require additional filesystem operations. [ R31 , R32 , R33 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, protection flags specify permitted reads, writes, and instruction execution.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 14: 36.6 Memory-mapped I/O

LECTURE NARRATION
The phrase memory-mapped I/O also describes device registers placed in an address map. Device mappings are not ordinary file-data mappings: accesses can have side effects, supported widths, ordering requirements, and cacheability constraints. A volatile pointer alone does not provide every device-ordering or synchronization guarantee. Device access must follow the operating system’s driver interfaces and architecture-specific requirements. This book’s user-space file-mapping labs do not access physical device registers.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
The program asks the operating system to move bytes to or from a resource, much like using a numbered ticket to ask a clerk for the right item.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 16: Worked example — A read-only mapped byte sum

LECTURE NARRATION
This Linux/POSIX utility accepts a regular-file path, handles the empty-file case, checks that the length fits size_t , maps read-only, and computes an unsigned 64-bit byte sum. The sum is a teaching checksum, not a cryptographic integrity mechanism. Companion listing: ch36/mapped_sum.c A file containing exactly ABC produces 198 because 65 + 66 + 67 = 198 on the stated ASCII-compatible reference environment. A binary fixture containing bytes 0, 1, 127, 128, and 255 produces 511. The test suite supplies controlled temporary files; it does not mutate an existing user document.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, this Linux/POSIX utility accepts a regular-file path, handles the empty-file case, checks that the length fits size_t , maps read-only, and computes an unsigned 64-bit byte sum.

SLIDE 18: Worked example — Summing a mapped file

LECTURE NARRATION
Map a read-only file region with mmap , then treat the mapped bytes as memory within the valid range. The first access to a page may fault so the kernel can establish a page backed by file data. Subsequent accesses can proceed through ordinary load instructions. Unmapping ends the virtual mapping, not the file’s existence.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SLIDE 20: Worked example — Private versus shared mapping

LECTURE NARRATION
With a private writable file mapping, a process can modify its page without necessarily updating the underlying file; copy-on-write supplies private pages. With a shared mapping, permitted writes can propagate to the file-backed shared state. The mapping flags therefore define visibility semantics, not merely performance.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, with a private writable file mapping, a process can modify its page without necessarily updating the underlying file; copy-on-write supplies private pages.

Do not truncate a live mapping as an ordinary test; analyze that failure contract instead. Review 1. Why is mapping == NULL the wrong failure test? Review 2. Why does a stable-file assumption matter even after a successful fstat ?

SLIDE 24: Chapter Synthesis

LECTURE NARRATION
The chapter's central subject is memory-mapped files. Correct reasoning requires explicit assumptions, bounds, ownership, and interface contracts. Observed behavior is evidence about a run; it is not automatically a language or system guarantee. Use the worked examples and lab to test whether the model transfers to new cases.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true.
